account: RL-Math's weight change is small (0.24 % of weight norm) and, like any RL run's, concentrated in each matrix's top 8 singular directions (top-8 share 0.118-0.135 Math, 0.127 for LM-judge RL, 0.030 Think-SFT); those 8 input-output pairs carry the gain: base + 1.5x them matches RL per sample (hard328 0.642 vs 0.640, MATH-500 456 vs 457, fresh2026 48.25 vs 50.5 of 136) and under a 4-vote (216.3 vs 215.9 of 328), the extra 0.5x standing in for the other 88 % of the change, while equal-norm random, Think-SFT or pair-shifted rank-8 edits do nothing because the base's later layers amplify only RL's own pairs (3-6x random).

The pairs hold three separable parts: a deliberative opening (late-MLP directions that read Okay/Wait/consider; the plain top-8 edit 427 vs random 197 of 500), a finishing part in direction 1 and layers 22-31 that cuts hard328 cap hits (20 % to 11-13 %, 5 % at 3x) but does not raise, and when enlarged lowers, the right rate of finished answers (0.63 at 1.5x, 0.51 at 3x, 0.41 at 4.5x), and an accuracy part in directions 2-8 and layers 0-10 that raises the finished right rate (0.63 to 0.73-0.79) while leaving cap hits at 19-25 %; only finishing plus accuracy together give RL's 0.64.

The opening is what the three-token cue gives the untrained base: at RL step 100 the plain model scores like the cued base (417.5 vs 410.5 of 500), hits the cap as often and gains as much from a vote (+7.2 vs +7.6 points), and a plain-base answer that opens deliberatively is right as often as a cued one, so the cue alone buys 79 % of RL's MATH-500 gain (224 to 410.5, RL 460) while steps 100-2,800 add the finishing and accuracy parts (+42.5 of 500).

The accuracy part lowers the per-step slip rate on every sample, including problems the base cannot solve: on hard328 problems where the cued base finished wrong the edit is right 36 % vs 23 % for a second base sample, and on problems the cued base gets 0 of 4 it captures 0.88 [0.69, 1.13] of RL's per-sample gain; on code, Code-RL's own pairs do this (+7 points pass among finished answers over random) and Math's do not (+1.5), though their extra passes fall on problems the base already passes in other samples.

Inference changes reach this part only by selection and loop removal: T 1.0 removes the T 0.6 loops (52-63 % of long attempts), and because the cued base's wrong answers scatter (same-problem agreement 0.26) a vote over 4 adds about 7 points on MATH-500 (446-450 vs RL 460) and lifts hard328 from 161 to 195 of 328, but the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins and more tokens or loop-neuron zeroing finish answers without making them right, so about 9 points on hard328 (195 vs 224) stay out of inference reach.

Hence new edit cells follow which part they carry, not their norm or module type: edits confined to direction 1 or layers 22-31 cut cap hits and lower finished accuracy as they grow, edits confined to directions 2-8 or layers 0-10 raise finished accuracy to about 0.75-0.80 on hard328 at the base's cap rate of about 0.2, any edit holding both at 1.25-1.5x lands within 3 points of RL per sample and per vote on every set, including problems the base never solves, and random, pair-shifted or Think-SFT rank-8 edits stay at the base.
